s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction with highly vascularized mass
salient_findings: Voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
Hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
key_facts: Woman in her 30s with no relevant medical history
Progressive bilateral nasal airway obstruction
Endoscopic examination found a voluminous, pulsatile, highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities
CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity, on the left thyroid, the fifth rib, and the L4 vertebra
MRI confirmed a hypervascular tumor with anterior skull base extension
Radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions
Sinonasal tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy
Serum thyroglobulin significantly elevated at 4432 ng/mL
Biopsy results pointed to vascular thyroid carcinoma metastasis

shortlist.label: Vascular Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Biopsy results pointed to vascular thyroid carcinoma metastasis and serum thyroglobulin significantly elevated

shortlist.label: Metastatic Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: CT scan showed a hypervascular tumor in the nasal cavity and radioiodine scintigraphy found considerable uptake regarding rib and vertebral lesions

shortlist.label: Metastatic Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Elevated serum thyroglobulin and metastatic disease in the nasal cavity, ribs, and vertebrae

shortlist.label: Radioiodine-refractory vesicular thyroid carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy of the sinonasal tumor and significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin

shortlist.label: Metastatic Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma
shortlist.why_kept: Aggressive disease with metastasis to the nasal cavity, ribs, and vertebrae, and significantly elevated serum thyroglobulin

raw.rationale: The biopsy results pointed to vascular thyroid carcinoma metastasis, and the patient's serum thyroglobulin was significantly elevated, which is consistent with a thyroid carcinoma diagnosis. The presence of a highly vascularized mass in both nasal cavities and the findings on imaging studies also support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Metastatic Follicular Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: While follicular thyroid carcinoma can be highly vascular, the biopsy results specifically pointed to vascular thyroid carcinoma metastasis.

rejected.label: Metastatic Papillary Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: Papillary thyroid carcinoma is the most common type of thyroid cancer, but the biopsy results and clinical presentation are more consistent with vascular thyroid carcinoma.

rejected.label: Radioiodine-refractory vesicular thyroid carcinoma
rejected.why: The patient's tumor had low uptake on radioiodine scintigraphy, but this is not sufficient to classify it as radioiodine-refractory.

rejected.label: Metastatic Poorly Differentiated Thyroid Carcinoma
rejected.why: There is no specific evidence in the case to suggest poorly differentiated thyroid carcinoma.
